chapter: Leading his own band in Los Angeles
title: Elected leader of the Harlem Gentlemen; Paramount and Pantages
summary: The band voted Clayton leader over Jack Bratton; they played the Paramount with the Mills Brothers and the Pantages circuit up the coast.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well after that we decided to elect somebody in the band, rather than give up the band. And they had my name and another trumpet player Jack Bratton.
Yes. Between us, they were going to elect a new leader. So I got more votes than Jack did, so I became the leader of Harlem Gentlemen from ). (LAUGHTER).

And oh, there were things, we had a lot of, a lot of things happened shortly after I took over the band. We were booked in the Paramount Theater, with the Mills Brothers when they first were beginning. They had been singing, but this was in their early, early days.
We were booked in the Paramount. And then I played Pantages circuit with Rosco Ates. I don't know if you know him or not.
Rosco Ates, yes, Rosco Ates. He used to spell it all the time, a comedian.
Oh no, I don't know him.
Yes, we played the, played the Pantages.
Yes. All the way from Los Angeles up to Vancouver.
Oh I see. You stayed on the West Coast?
Well what sort of places were you
That must have been, I mean the clicking band must have been then?

Yes. We had a pretty good band. We had a pretty good band I thought. And we did very, very nicely. Very nicely. And as I say, we played Frisco. All up and down the Coast. We played a lot of night clubs too.
So we stayed together for quite a while playing in and around Los Angeles.
Well I mean how long when you say quite a while? Was that two years or a year?
